newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OLYMPICS-S.AFRICAN BID CITY COURTS ASIAN VOTE.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-S.AFRICAN BID CITY COURTS ASIAN VOTE.

text.p: Cape Town's Olympic Bid company is making a concerted attempt to woo the Asian vote to clinch the 2004 games.
The bid company's director of international affairs, Ntsundeni Madzunya, told a press briefing on Tuesday that Asia would be crucial to the city's chances.
"We hope the base of Cape Town's support and the core of it will come from Africa and Asia," he said on his return from a six-nation tour of Asia.
Madzunya spoke to six Asian International Olympic Committee (IOC) members and will visit both Koreas, China and Japan at the start of July to speak to a further six.
Cape Town officials expect to have met all 18 IOC members from Asia by the end of July.
"They told us we should not be worried about the technical side of the Cape Town bid, but rather we should be telling them what was different about us from the rest of the bidders," said Madzunya.
"We told them this was the only bid that would increase the quality of life, its people and, indeed, of the whole continent.
"I have a good feeling from the advice they have given us about other IOC members in Asia."

At the same briefing Lamine Diack, the Senegalese vice-president of the International Amateur Athletics Federation and president of the African Athletics Confederation, reaffirmed his support for the bid.
"I will be on your side, working to convince the IOC to vote for Cape Town in September. This bid is an African one," he said. "Most or all of the African IOC members will be backing you."
